findings.claim: safePattern only refuses a Glob pattern that starts with '/', '~' or '$' or holds '..'. A brace pattern such as '{/etc/*,x}' or '{~/.ssh/*,a}' passes, and Glob is allowed with no path. If the Glob tool expands braces before resolving the pattern against the search directory, the absolute alternative lists files outside the root. Whether Claude Code's Glob expands braces into absolute roots was not checked. D1 has no brace row.

The root is call.Cwd, the hook input's cwd, which L43 found is the session's current directory, not a per-agent value. A parent, or a sibling agent sharing the session cwd, that runs 'cd <other repo>' moves the root, and Write and the script are then allowed on <other repo>/docs/wiki/evidence.md, the cross-project write -3 F3 and -5 F2 asked to close. Whether Claude Code keeps the main thread's cwd after a cd was not checked.

README says the root is 'the directory the classifier was launched in' and the ScopedToolCall comment calls cwd 'the working directory of the agent whose call is judged'; L43 records that the hook's cwd is the parent session's launch directory. In this workflow the foreman runs in the dev checkout, so the guard ties the classifier to the dev checkout's page, not the worktree's.

The 'cannot decode' assertion picks its row by position, failures[len(failures)-3]; a row added later moves it silently and the test would stop proving that a repeated key with the allowed last value is refused by decoding. Name the row.
